extracted.intended_audience: researchers and methodologists conducting systematic reviews and Health Technology Assessment (HTA) studies; reviewers assessing dissemination/publication bias
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and data-extraction/checklist templates for identifying, categorising, and critically appraising dissemination (publication) bias in empirical, methodological studies and in samples of published systematic reviews. Includes classification of biases, methods, the stages at which methods apply, and quality-assessment items for studies and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific rigorousness (empirical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific rigorousness of empirical evidence studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: prospective or retrospective design, sample selection bias; to be critically appraised in terms of scientific rigorousness as part of overall appraisal for direct-evidence studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the study sample is representative of the population/field of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: consider research field, participants, outcomes, interventions, and study designs when assessing representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the data analysis used in the study is appropriate given objectives and available data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: consider the study objectives, available data and methods of data analysis when appraising appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors' interpretation of results is appropriate and takes study limitations into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: limitations of the study should be taken into consideration when judging interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of methods — underlying assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess methods in terms of their underlying assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each method identified, document what assumptions it relies on as part of critical appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of methods — conditions for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the conditions under which a method could be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document contexts or stages of review where method is applicable (e.g., before/during/after literature review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of methods — usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the practical usefulness of the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include empirical evidence of usefulness where available and judge how useful the method would be in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of methods — limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Document limitations of the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State known limitations, potential biases introduced, and conditions where the method performs poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of methods — resources required
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate resources (time, staff, cost) required to use the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State resource implications based on literature and experience; include time, staff, and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of empirical study results
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorise empirical evidence study results as positive, non-significant, or can't tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive = significant dissemination bias; Non-significant = no clear dissemination bias; Can't tell = insufficient information. Use these categories for synthesis and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association with study quality and dissemination profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine association between empirical study results and study quality/dissemination profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissemination profile includes time of publication, journal impact factor, number of citations after a given period, and study's impact on guidelines/recommendations for systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method inventory by method investigated
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate a list of available methods and corresponding studies identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorise methodological studies according to the methods they investigated to compile an inventory and map evidence to methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-classify methods by dissemination bias type
rubrics_metrics.description: For each method, indicate the type(s) of dissemination bias it addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types include publication bias, language bias, abstract bias, database index bias, duplicate bias, grey literature bias, reporting bias, time delay bias, citation bias, media attention bias, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-classify methods by stage of literature review
rubrics_metrics.description: For each method, indicate the stage of the literature review where it applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stages: before literature review, in literature review, after literature review. A method may be relevant to multiple stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardised method classification sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a standardised method classification sheet for documenting methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided classification sheet (Appendix 2) to ensure consistent documentation across method studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-reviewer data extraction and checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Data extraction and categorisation to be done independently by two reviewers where specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For empirical evidence studies and systematic reviews, extraction is independently conducted by two reviewers; disagreements resolved by discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of findings — tables and narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Present extracted data and critical appraisal results in tables and narratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise methods, findings, and appraisal results in tables with accompanying narrative description; consider quantitative pooling where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative pooling where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Pool results quantitatively when appropriate (e.g., pooled odds ratio of full publication of conference abstracts with significant vs non-significant results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make pooling decisions considering heterogeneity and the results of critical appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare new findings with previous HTA report
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight whether new findings contradict or strengthen findings from the previous HTA report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss consistency or change over time, and implications for practice and resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frame for systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain a representative random sample of systematic reviews from MEDLINE categorized into types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories: (1) systematic reviews of effects of healthcare interventions, (2) of accuracy of diagnostic tests, (3) epidemiological association reviews (including genetic). Use computer-generated random numbers to select target sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracted data items from systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract key items: type of review, method of data synthesis, whether publication bias was considered, searches for unpublished/non-English studies, methods used to deal with publication bias, evidence on existence/extent/consequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary data extraction sheet (Appendix 3) and code items consistently; extract sufficient detail to judge practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality checklist for systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a checklist to assess overall quality of included systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Appendix 3 checklist items (seven items listed below); apply independently by two reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well defined review question (SR quality item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the systematic review has a well defined review question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate: Yes / Partially / No / Can't tell.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of all relevant studies (SR quality item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the systematic review identified all relevant studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate: Yes / Partially / No / Can't tell; consider comprehensiveness of search sources and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate assessment of study quality (SR quality item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review appropriately assessed the quality of included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate: Yes / Partially / No / Can't tell; consider risk-of-bias tools or other quality appraisal methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliable and accurate data extraction (SR quality item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether data extraction in the review was reliable and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate: Yes / Partially / No / Can't tell; consider processes such as duplicate extraction and checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate investigation of heterogeneity (SR quality item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review appropriately investigated differences between studies (heterogeneity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate: Yes / Partially / No / Can't tell; consider use of statistical tests, meta-regression, subgroup or sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate data synthesis (SR quality item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review used appropriate methods to synthesise data (narrative or quantitative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate: Yes / Partially / No / Can't tell; consider choice between narrative synthesis and meta-analysis given data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate interpretation of results (SR quality item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether interpretations and conclusions are appropriate given the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate: Yes / Partially / No / Can't tell; consider whether limitations and potential biases are acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical study issues to record
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the primary issues the empirical study addresses: existence/identifying, consequence, causes/risk factors, or other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tick applicable items on data extraction sheet to characterise study focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of dissemination problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify dissemination problems: non-publication, limited accessibility, incomplete publication, other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to describe the type of dissemination problem studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific bias types (classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify specific bias types examined: publication bias, language bias, abstract bias, database index bias, duplicate bias, other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record each specific bias type studied; allows mapping of methods to particular biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias 'areas' to record
rubrics_metrics.description: Record bias areas such as grey literature bias, reporting bias, time delay bias, citation bias, media attention bias, general health or specific health topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these area categories to contextualise bias within topic areas or dissemination mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence type: direct vs indirect
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify evidence as direct or indirect and proceed accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For indirect evidence, stop detailed direct-evidence appraisal. For direct evidence, continue with rigorous appraisal fields (scientific rigorousness, sample representativeness, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall study quality rating (empirical studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate overall scientific quality of empirical evidence studies as High, Moderate, Low, or Can't tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: 'High' = without considerable concern on study validity; 'Moderate' = some concern; 'Low' = considerable concern. Use this after appraising design, analysis, interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological study classification — method types
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the method(s) investigated in methodological studies (e.g., study registration, funnel plot, updating reviews, research ethics/policy, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note method categories such as literature search, statistical/modelling, publication process, confirmatory studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological study purpose classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Record purpose of the method: preventing bias, reducing bias, detecting bias, adjusting bias, or other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps map methods to intended function in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage of literature review for methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the method applies before the review, during the review, or after the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark all applicable stages; some methods operate across multiple stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources required for methods (methodological studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document resources required to implement the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include time, staff, and cost estimates, based on study report or reviewer experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer’s commentary (methodological studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reviewer commentary on study validity, scientific rigorousness, method usefulness and limitations, and any empirical evidence provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use free-text reviewer comments to summarise critical judgements and caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic review classification items
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify systematic reviews by topic/type: genetic epidemiology, effectiveness/adverse effects, diagnostic, other epidemiology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use classification to stratify sampling and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of review synthesis — meta-analysis vs narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the systematic review used meta-analysis or narrative synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare findings and treatment of publication bias between types of synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs of included studies (SR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record designs of studies included in the systematic review (RCTs/CCTs, diagnostic accuracy studies, epidemiological studies, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This informs applicability of bias-detection methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: How differences between studies were investigated (SR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record methods used to investigate between-study differences: NA, narrative, statistical, meta-regression, sensitivity/subgroup, other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use checkboxes provided in the extraction sheet; document details of analyses performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of authors' conclusions (SR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the systematic review authors' conclusions as significant/positive, non-significant/not important, or unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide brief interpretation: e.g., 'At least one intervention recommended' for positive, 'No intervention recommended' for non-significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources searched and reporting of non-English/unpublished studies (SR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record which sources were searched (MEDLINE, EMBASE, handsearch, experts, Cochrane, proceedings, company, etc.) and status of non-English and unpublished studies (searched/identified/included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document search methods, how many non-English/unpublished studies were found, and whether they were included in primary or sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue of publication bias discussed (SR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether the systematic review discussed publication bias (Yes/No) and the methods used to address it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discussed, document methods used (prospective register, funnel plot, Egger’s method, modelling, fail-safe N, rank correlation, identify unpublished studies, large trials, other) and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence on publication bias in SRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether evidence on publication bias was available and details if so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: comparisons of published vs unpublished trials, funnel plot shapes, results of bias tests.
